cross-013.answer: Skiff runs Tern at the Performance preset, which saves 1.8 ms over Quality (2.1 ms vs 3.9 ms), per `dec-run-tern-on-skiff-at-the-performance-preset--74eqayfa83ybqpe3`.

cross-015.answer: Two Efforts are no longer active. Shader compile cache and build farm is completed (status only; I found no closing record saying every farm build reads from the cache). Co-op rollback netcode prototype was abandoned by dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b, which stops rollback because re-running tides on every rollback frame costs 4.8 ms on Skiff.

netcode-004.answer: The team abandoned rollback netcode for co-op because re-running the tide simulation on every rolled-back frame costs 4.8 ms on Skiff, about a fifth of the 25 ms frame, and shrinking the window and quarter-resolution tides both failed (dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b). The reason depends on the world Decision dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e, which keeps tides deterministic.

ports-012.answer: The ports team raised the Skiff dynamic resolution floor to 576p because saltglass caustics shimmered badly in motion at the 540p floor (visible in 7 of 10 dune views, versus 2 of 10 at 576p), and 576p still fit the 33.3 ms budget at 30 Hz (dec-raise-the-skiff-dynamic-resolution-floor-to-576p--fep9q7m08pp9f0bb). That decision was later superseded by dec-lower-the-skiff-dynamic-resolution-floor-to-504p--15esnt90gcn29enn, which lowered the floor to 504p behind Tern.

ports-013.answer: Ship Tern as Lantern's only upscaler

render-031.answer: dec-visibility-buffer-for-opaque-geometry-foliage-an--gvnvp04jgm7kbfh9: alpha-tested foliage cost 2.1 ms in the visibility buffer versus 0.8 ms in forward+, and saltglass refracts the already-resolved scene so it cannot live in the buffer.

render-032.answer: The team chose Tern because Halcyon has no Skiff build, and shipping Halcyon on two platforms would break the one-upscaler constraint; owning the Tern code also suits saltglass refraction and caustics better than vendor tickets and a license negotiation would (dec-ship-tern-as-lantern-s-only-upscaler--fmreq35nzyjc7k4e).

render-046.answer: The 3.1 ms cost finding that rejected them (fnd-virtual-shadow-maps-cost-3-1-ms-on-meridian--r6x0sdfecms7j1yg) was a capture error: the debug flag discarded cached pages. With caching, VSM costs 1.4 ms, less than four cascades' 1.6 ms, and CSM's cascade seams through saltglass remain unsolved; see dec-use-virtual-shadow-maps-for-the-sun--x8nqkn9q7eaf1ap4.

render-047.answer: Because the release-build capture puts the visibility buffer at 7.4 ms on Skiff against 8.1 ms for forward+ (6.3 ms with material resolve at half rate), so the forward+ fallback is no longer worth keeping, and keeping two opaque paths cost about one engineer-week a month in fixes. dec-visibility-buffer-on-all-platforms-skiff-resolve--k1ackk3c3275r5y1

world-011.answer: Closed as wontfix: the Name component was not shipped in release builds because it would cost 57 MB at full population. Instead, the crash pipeline maps entity numbers back to names from the build symbol file. Resolving record: fnd-shipping-entity-names-costs-57-mb-at-full-popula--6w7gjvy7wdmdx9qx

world-036.answer: Kestrel retired fibers because 41% of alpha crash reports had no usable stack, which blocked crash triage for beta, and a thread pool with continuation waits kept workers 93% busy during tide turns, close to the 95% fibers gave (dec-return-engine-jobs-to-a-thread-pool-with-continu--1zkc1v2x97taf50h).

world-051.answer: The tide simulation moved to 32.32 fixed point so that tide state is bit-identical on every CPU and compiler; float tides drifted apart between machines within 6 minutes, and integer math avoids that where strict IEEE mode would not. The strict IEEE option was rejected in favor of it (`dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e`).

world-055.answer: Kelp stays because dec-shrink-kelp-s-dictionary-to-1-mb-for-streamed-as--yh8hktfqnyqhepew found that Kelp with a 1 MB dictionary still beats Zstandard cold on Skiff, and it closed the reopened Zstandard option. That decision's 1.7x figure is out of date: the later finding fnd-kelp-with-a-1-mb-dictionary-decodes-at-1-5-gb-s--y9v8jrxgbv6abrx5 puts Kelp's lead at 1.25x.
